0.headline: Vijay Kedia-backed Asuthosh Fibre draws Rs 16 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
0.heading: Vijay Kedia-backed Asuthosh Fibre draws Rs 16 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
0.intro: Asuthosh Fibre IPO | The company is looking to raise Rs 56.34 crore through an initial public offering of 61.24 lakh shares.
0.body:
Gujarat-based Asuthosh Fibre, a manufacturer and trader of technical textile products backed by well-known investor Vijay Kishanlal Kedia, has raised Rs 16.04 crore from five anchor investors, including Madhusudan Kela-mentored Singularity AMC, on August 28, a day before the IPO opens for public subscription.

The company is looking to raise Rs 56.34 crore through an initial public offering (IPO) of 61.24 lakh shares, comprising entirely a fresh issue. The price band for the offer has been fixed at Rs 87–92 per share.

The IPO will open for public subscription on August 31 and close on September 2.

Asuthosh Fibre has allocated 17.43 lakh shares through the anchor book at the upper end of the price band.

Nine Alps Corporate Advisors picked up 6.52 lakh shares for Rs 6 crore, while Singularity Equity Fund II and Nav Capital Emerging Star Fund each bought 3.75 lakh shares for Rs 3.45 crore.

Further, Aarth AIF Growth Fund acquired 2.3 lakh shares valued at Rs 2.11 crore, while Vira Bharat Opportunities Fund picked up 1.09 lakh shares for Rs 1 crore.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The yarn and fabric manufacturer and trader will utilise Rs 25.5 crore of the net offer proceeds to fund new equipment and machinery, Rs 20 crore for debt repayment and the remaining proceeds for general corporate purposes.

Promoters hold a 59.79 percent stake in the company on a pre-offer paid-up equity basis, while the remaining shares are held by public shareholders, including Vijay Kishanlal Kedia, who held a 6.57 percent stake.

On the financial front, Asuthosh Fibre reported a profit of Rs 16.04 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, an 88.5 percent increase from Rs 8.5 crore in the previous year. Revenue during the same period increased 2.9 percent to Rs 117.37 crore from Rs 114 crore.

Mefcom Capital Markets has been appointed as the merchant banker for managing the Asuthosh Fibre IPO.

1.headline: Sumex Engineering IPO subscribed 152 times on final day, GMP spikes to around 35%
1.heading: Sumex Engineering IPO subscribed 152 times on final day, GMP spikes to around 35%
1.intro: Sumex Engineering IPO | The company is expected to finalise the IPO share allotment by August 31, while trading in its equity shares is likely to commence on the NSE Emerge platform on September 2.
1.body:
Telangana-based Sumex Engineering's initial public offering (IPO) attracted robust demand across investor categories, with the issue subscribed 151.74 times on August 28, the final day of bidding.

The company, which manufactures products for automobile companies, is raising Rs 53.4 crore through the initial share sale of 52.87 lakh shares at the upper end of the price band of Rs 95–101 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 42.91 lakh shares, while promoters are offloading 9.96 lakh shares through an offer for sale (OFS).

Investors placed bids for 58.44 crore shares over the four-day bidding period from August 25 to 28, against the offer size of 38.52 lakh shares, through 1.37 lakh applications.

Non-institutional investors took the lead, bidding 271.06 times their allotted quota, while the portions reserved for retail investors and qualified institutional buyers were subscribed 159 times and 121.28 times, respectively.

Sumex Engineering is expected to finalise the IPO share allotment by August 31, while trading in its equity shares is likely to commence on the NSE Emerge platform on September 2.

Sumex shares were trading at around a 35 percent premium in the grey market, according to market observers. The grey market is an unofficial market for trading in IPO shares before their listing on the stock exchanges.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

With two existing manufacturing facilities in Tamil Nadu and Haryana, the company manufactures and trades in products tailored for the automotive industry. Its product portfolio includes adhesive tapes and die-cuts, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing pads, reflective tapes and printing solutions, domes and graphics, as well as a range of car care products.

Sumex intends to set up two additional manufacturing facilities in Rajasthan and Haryana using the IPO proceeds.

Of the net fresh issue proceeds, Rs 4.88 crore will be utilised for the construction of a manufacturing unit in Rajasthan, while Rs 16.62 crore will be used for the construction of a unit in Haryana.

Further, Rs 12 crore will be used for working capital requirements, while the remaining proceeds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.

GYR Capital Advisors is acting as the merchant banker for the public issue of Sumex Engineering.

2.headline: Purple Style Labs IPO to open on Aug 31; 8 investors pick up Rs 306 crore worth shares via anchor book
2.heading: Purple Style Labs IPO to open on Aug 31; 8 investors pick up Rs 306 crore worth shares via anchor book
2.intro: Purple Style Labs IPO | The Abhishek Agarwal-promoted company is looking to raise up to Rs 680 crore through an initial public offering, comprising entirely a fresh issue.
2.body:
Purple Style Labs, the Mumbai-based luxury fashion company operating 14 stores under the Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop brand, has raised Rs 306 crore from eight anchor investors, including Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities and Integrated Core Strategies, on August 28.

The fundraising comes ahead of the IPO opening for public subscription on August 31. The price band has been fixed at Rs 546–575 per share, and the issue will close on September 2.

The Abhishek Agarwal-promoted company is looking to raise up to Rs 680 crore through an initial public offering (IPO), comprising entirely a fresh issue.

Purple Style Labs has allocated 53.21 lakh shares through the anchor book at the upper end of the price band on Friday.

Of the total anchor book, 17.39 lakh shares were allocated to two domestic mutual funds, which applied through three schemes. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerged as the largest buyer among anchor investors, picking up 15.3 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 88 crore.

This was followed by Jupiter Asset Management, which bought over 13 lakh shares worth Rs 75 crore, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, which purchased 11.82 lakh shares worth Rs 68 crore.

Ace investor Madhusudan Kela-backed Singularity AMC acquired an additional 1.73 lakh shares in Purple Style Labs worth nearly Rs 10 crore, while ITI Mutual Fund bought over 2 lakh shares worth Rs 12 crore.

Singularity AMC already held a 1.86 percent stake in the fashion company, while Akash Bhanshali-sponsored Volrado Venture Partners and Mukul Mahavir Agrawal held 2.79 percent and 1.37 percent stakes, respectively. Promoter Abhishek Agarwal owns a 26.09 percent stake in the company.

Purple Style Labs provides curated selections of luxury fashion sourced from 1,109 active designer brands, including Seema Gujral, Anushree Reddy, Amit Aggarwal, and Rohit Gandhi &amp; Rahul Khanna, across women’s wear, men’s wear and other categories, with a focus on wedding and occasion wear.

The company intends to invest Rs 371.1 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds in its subsidiary, PSL Retail, towards expenditure on lease liabilities for Experience Centers and back-end offices in India.

Further, Rs 138.9 crore will be utilised for sales and marketing expenses, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company operates through 14 Experience Centers globally, including 12 in metropolitan cities across India, which are operated on a leave-and-license basis. It also sells through online platforms and participates in events and exhibitions.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are acting as the merchant bankers for the public issue of Purple Style Labs.
